$comment: ENGAGEMENT.md C7 — the framing rule, made mechanical.
Sezer/Gino/Norton (JPSP) found that humblebragging leaves people LESS liked
and less trusted than plain bragging, and that self-promoters systematically
overestimate how well their sharing lands. For an NGO whose subject is free
public sport in a country where 61% never exercise, copy that frames a
member as better than other members is both off-message and, by that
evidence, less effective at the thing it is for.
So achievement and share copy is framed around SHOWING UP and BELONGING TO A
PLACE — '50 тренировки', 'Господар на Южен парк' — never around superiority.
This file is the denylist that keeps it that way; the gate is
apps/web/tests/framing.test.ts.
WHY JSON RATHER THAN TypeScript: the hardcoded-Cyrillic gate scans every .ts
and .tsx under apps/web/{app,components,lib} with an empty allowlist, so a
Bulgarian denylist written in TypeScript would be flagged as hardcoded UI
copy by the very gate it sits beside. Message data lives in .json here.
WHY WORD BOUNDARIES, NOT SUBSTRINGS: calibrating this list against the live
catalogue caught 'елит' matching inside 'Сателитен изглед'. Bulgarian is
agglutinative enough that substring matching produces confident nonsense, so
every token below is matched at a word boundary and stems are marked.
This list is deliberately about COMPARISON BETWEEN MEMBERS. It does not
forbid naming a campaign winner or printing a rank — those are facts on a
ranking surface, which is why Leaderboard and Campaign are outside the
gate's scope (see the test).
